entities.name: Saint Aurelius
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aurelius of Carthage was a Christian saint who died around 430. He was bishop of Carthage from about 391 until his death and is remembered for his role in the early development of Christianity.

Born into a pagan family, Aurelius converted to Christianity during the reign of Emperor Theodosius I (r. 378-392 CE). His conversion was likely influenced by the teachings of Saint Ambrose, who would later become bishop of Milan and play a significant role in shaping Christian doctrine.

Aurelius's leadership in Carthage helped to establish the city as a center of Christian learning and culture. He was a close friend and mentor to Saint Augustine of Hippo, with whom he shared a deep love of theology and literature.

The legacy of Aurelius can be seen in the continued influence of his teachings on Christian doctrine and practice. His example has inspired countless saints, bishops, and theologians throughout history, including many prominent figures in the Catholic Church.

"The Church is not made by human hands, but it is adorned with the blood of martyrs," Aurelius once said. This profound statement captures the essence of his commitment to the faith and his role as a model for Christian leaders everywhere.
